chapter: Woody Herman, Condon's and Buddy Rich
title: Joining Woody Herman and the 1976 Carnegie Hall anniversary concert
summary: After more Gap Mangione he joins Woody Herman, plays La Fiesta again, and shares the drum chair with Jake Hanna and Don Lamond at Carnegie Hall.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Wow. Well how was Woody Herman different?

All right. I came back, after Maynard’s band, went back with Gap Mangione for another year. Then Woody Herman’s band called and I went with that band. And that band was an exciting band. It was one of the bands I wanted to play with. I had played “La Fiesta” with Maynard Ferguson for two years, and now I’m back playing “La Fiesta” with Woody Herman for another two years, which is basically a slightly different version because it doesn’t have all of the high, featuring Maynard and that. But like “Four Brothers,” “Early Autumn,” all of that stuff. All of those things. But the high point of being with that band was the Carnegie Hall concert we did, which was a 40th anniversary concert. I really enjoyed — I mean everybody was there, Stan, all of them, the whole thing, in 1976. They made a record on RCA of the 40th Anniversary Concert Live at Carnegie Hall. And I was loaded for that one too. But I enjoyed it. And Jake, the three drummers, with me, Jake Hanna and Don Lamond. I’ve got a picture of the three of us together. We shared the drum chairs on that.
Jake, he was a pistol, huh?
